name: tests-typecheck
description: TEST-SUITE TYPE CHECKING. tsconfig.json excludes `**/*.test.ts` and never included `tests/**`, so 700+ files and ~9,200 tests were type-checked by nothing — and a test is the worst place to lose it, because a type error there is invisible at runtime too (`expect(x.nonExistentField).toBeUndefined()` passes forever, and an import of a removed symbol only fails if the line executes). Unit 101 hit exactly that. Counted by scripts/check-tests-typecheck.mjs over tsconfig.tests.json, bidirectional, down-only.
lastBumpNote: SEEDED at 162 on 2026-08-14, which is 8 below the 170 first measured because the seeding commit also fixed five test files importing `../../../server/...` — one level too many, resolving outside the repo. Vite clamps paths above root so they resolved at RUNTIME and the suite was green; tsc was right and nothing had been asking it. A sixth finding came from the same pass and is not in this count because it was a SYNTAX error: tests/simulation/sim-scaling-operator.spec.ts used regex literals as object KEYS, which is not valid JavaScript, so the file never parsed and `npm run test:scale` had never run once. AND A CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: the first measurement of this population came back as TWELVE, from a scratchpad config outside the repo that could not resolve node/vite/vitest types, so tsc bailed early. I nearly recorded 'the suite type-checks clean'. The evaluator now refuses to report a count at all if it sees `Cannot find type definition file for`, because a gate that answers zero when it cannot look is worse than no gate. The remaining 162 are mostly mocks that cannot represent what they are asserted against (TS2493 on empty-tuple fixtures, TS2352/TS2322 on hand-built rows standing in for Drizzle types) — real friction, no live bugs, so a ratchet rather than a hard gate.
